title: Aaron Donald ends retirement, signs with Rams on 1-year, $20 million deal
dek: The defensive tackle, who sat out two seasons after retiring in March 2024, signed a one-year contract worth $20 million with an additional $10 million available in incentives. He reunites with newly acquired pass-rusher Myles Garrett as the Rams prepare for their September 10 season-opener in Melbourne, Australia.
author: The GoCheckMySports Desk
key_fact: Aaron Donald signed a one-year, $20 million deal with the Los Angeles Rams on August 30, 2026, ending a two-year retirement.
bottom_line: Donald's debut timeline remains uncertain. McVay's statement on August 30 that the team will take readiness one day at a time signals no commitment to Donald's availability by September 10, meaning the Rams may field their pass rush against San Francisco without him despite the contract signing.
body: An all-time defensive talent exited a two-year retirement on August 30 to pair with superstar pass-rusher Myles Garrett, reshaping the Rams' defensive line depth on the eve of the regular season. Aaron Donald signed a one-year, $20 million contract with the Los Angeles Rams, per Yahoo Sports, with an additional $10 million available in incentives.

Donald announced his retirement on March 15, 2024, and missed the last two seasons. According to Yahoo Sports, he had tallied 111 sacks over 154 games at the time of his retirement. In his final season before stepping away, Donald played 16 games, finishing with 53 total tackles and eight sacks.

The Rams acquired Myles Garrett via trade on June 1. Donald and Garrett now form a defensive line pairing after Donald's return. Head coach Sean McVay spoke to Donald about a return during Garrett's introductory press conference, per Yahoo Sports. Donald said he had known for two weeks that he was leaning toward returning and talked to McVay nearly every day, according to the same source.

Donald prepared for this moment during his retirement. According to Yahoo Sports, he said he had been locked in to training for the last 13 or 14 weeks and tested out his body to ensure he was physically able to play football. His wife, Erica, played a major part in the decision and gave her approval on social media, Yahoo Sports reports.

Donald was a member of the Rams squad that won the Super Bowl in 2022 with a 23-20 win over the Cincinnati Bengals. His Pro Football Hall of Fame eligibility has reset as a result of his return, according to Yahoo Sports; he will need to be out of the league for five years before being eligible for enshrinement once he officially retires again.

The Rams' season-opener is against the San Francisco 49ers in Melbourne, Australia, on September 10. McVay said on August 30 that they will take things one day at a time with Donald's readiness, per Yahoo Sports.
